findings.text: The landed diff removes _append_edges from nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py (renamed to _batch_edges with the different signature (sources, source_valid, targets, capacity)), but this tracked module still does 'from nova.equilibrium.contour_tree import ... _append_edges ...' at line 32 and calls it at line 155, so importing or running the benchmark now raises ImportError. The file is outside the node's declared write paths so the worker could not repair it, and no gate in the run imports it, which is why the break is silent.

The new receipt-identity guard sits under scripts/prototypes/, which pyproject's [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths does not collect, so no repository gate runs it and a future regression in the seven receipt fields reddens nothing in the default lane. The same applies to the assertion added in scripts/prototypes/contour_tree_sweep_profile/test_profile.py.

The gate log's first line names REVISION=cd169244542ed6f8bacbcde8bb7bb4db864c4409, but the file it ran (test_brute_receipt_identity.py) does not exist at that revision; it was added 2 minutes later in 0f80a85c7. The revision header therefore names a tree the tested artifact is not in, so the log cannot be reconciled against the commit it cites.

the manifest's tests: field names a script path (.../gpu-recheck.sh) rather than the literal command a shell was handed, so a reader cannot re-run the gate from that line alone and must fall back to the log's own COMMAND= header.

VERDICT done_when: the done_when's three measures are the seven-field identity checks, one H200 four-rung measurement per carrier, and one suite job running both arms with fresh processes; the manifest records H200 job 1291092, the 8 repaired rows under gpu-recheck/rows, and suite job 1291093's base/after EXIT= lines in suite-recheck/base-suite.log and suite-recheck/after-suite.log.
